title: Are veneers painful? Pain levels, anesthesia and what is not normal
seoTitle: Are Veneers Painful? Pain at Each Step and After
description: What getting veneers feels like on a 0 to 10 scale: the injection, preparation, temporaries, bonding and the first week, plus the pain that is not normal.
author: Dr. Roger Ramos Navarro, DMD
imageAlt: A patient's relaxed hands on a cream blanket in the dental chair, headphones beside them and numbing gel on the tray
answer: Getting veneers is **not painful**. The only moment most patients feel is the **numbing injection**, a few seconds of pressure after a topical gel. Preparation is done under local anesthesia and, with **0.3 mm veneers**, stays in enamel, which has no nerve. Afterwards, expect **mild cold sensitivity for two or three days**, not pain. Pain that lingers, throbs or hits one tooth when you bite is not normal and is a quick fix.

sections.h2: Veneer pain on a 0 to 10 scale, step by step

blocks.p: "Painful" means different things to different people, so here is the week the way patients describe it to us afterwards, on the usual 0 to 10 scale where 0 is nothing and 10 is the worst pain imaginable. The timeline itself, visit by visit, is in [Do veneers hurt? The process, day by day](/blog/do-veneers-hurt); this article is about how much, and what to do when it is more than that.

blocks.p: Nothing in that table reaches the level of a filling that touches dentin, a wisdom-tooth extraction or a root canal. The reason is anatomy, not bravery: a 0.3 mm preparation stays in enamel, enamel has no nerve endings, and the nerve itself sits 2 to 3 mm further in. The [Cleveland Clinic's veneer guidance](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/treatments/23522-dental-veneers) puts it the same way: the procedure is done under local anesthesia and most people feel only mild sensitivity afterwards.

sections.h2: The injection is the only part most people feel

blocks.p: If there is a moment of discomfort in the whole week, it is the local anesthetic before preparation. We put a topical numbing gel on the gum first and wait, then inject slowly, which is what makes the difference between a pinch and a sting. Patients rate it a 2 or 3 for a few seconds. Then the area goes numb for two to three hours, your lip feels large, and the preparation itself registers as vibration and the sound of water.

If needles are the part you dread, say so when you send your photos. The gel is applied for longer, the injection is given even more slowly, and you can ask for a break or a signal to pause at any point. A few patients choose to have the preparation done without anesthetic because 0.3 mm in enamel does not reach the nerve; it is possible, but we would rather you were comfortable for three hours than proving a point.

blocks.quote: The most common thing patients say at the end of Visit 2 is that they were braced for something that never came. The injection was the whole event.

sections.h2: Why veneers hurt less than most dental work

blocks.p: Pain in dentistry tracks how close the work comes to the nerve and how much the surrounding tissue is disturbed. Veneers sit at the gentle end of that range, which surprises people who assume that anything cosmetic across 20 teeth must be a big procedure.

blocks.p: The practical point is the first row. How much a veneer hurts is decided by how much tooth is removed, and that is decided before you sit down, at the design visit. [Minimal prep versus no-prep veneers](/blog/minimal-prep-veneers-vs-no-prep-veneers) explains the numbers; ask any clinic you are comparing for theirs.

sections.h2: Anxiety is not pain, but it feels like it

blocks.p: Most of what patients call fear of pain is fear of not knowing what is coming. That is why the design visit matters for comfort as well as for the result: you see every step before it happens, you know the preparation visit is about three hours, and you know nothing is drilled until you have approved the design in your own mouth.

list: **Tell the team.** Anxiety noted on your plan changes how the visit is run: longer topical gel, slower pace, more explanation, scheduled breaks.
**Bring headphones.** Most of what people remember as unpleasant is the sound, not a sensation. Music or a podcast removes it.
**Agree a signal.** A raised hand stops everything, no questions asked. Knowing you can stop is usually enough never to need to.
**Eat beforehand.** Visit 2 is long and you will not want to chew for a few hours after. Low blood sugar makes everything feel worse.
**Ask about sedation if you need it.** Local anesthesia is enough for almost everyone, but if past dental experiences were bad, say so when you send your photos and we will plan the visit around it.

sections.h2: Pain after veneers: the first week

blocks.p: The first 72 hours after preparation, and again after bonding, are when sensitivity peaks. It is a short, sharp response to cold or sweet that fades in seconds, not an ache. Tender gums at the margin for a day or two are also normal; the tissue was retracted slightly for the impressions and the bonding.

steps: **Eat soft and lukewarm for two days.** Not because the veneers are fragile, but because cold and hard are what trigger the sensitivity you want to avoid.
**Use a sensitivity toothpaste** and a soft brush. Brush normally; skipping the margins makes the gums sorer, not better.
**An over-the-counter painkiller is enough** if you want one, taken as the label says. Most patients take none.
**Do not test the bite.** Tapping and grinding your teeth together to check how they feel is the fastest way to make a tender tooth sore.
**Wear the night guard from the first night** if you were given one. Grinding on new porcelain is a common reason for a sore jaw in the first week.

blocks.p: Flying home the evening of the bonding visit, as most out-of-state patients do, is fine. The [out-of-state patients page](/out-of-state-patients) has the week laid out, and your coordinator is a text away if anything feels off once you are home.

sections.h2: Pain that is not normal, and what it usually means

blocks.p: A small number of patients have pain that does not fit the pattern above. Almost always it has a mechanical cause that takes minutes to fix, and it is covered by the warranty. Call the same day rather than waiting for it to settle.

blocks.p: None of these are reasons to live with pain and none are the patient's fault. A veneer that hurts weeks after delivery is a veneer that needs a five-minute adjustment, and the ceramist and the doctor who placed it are in the same building. The [warranty article](/blog/veneer-warranty-what-it-covers) explains what is covered and for how long.

No. Porcelain has no nerve and does not become sensitive with age. When a veneered tooth hurts years after delivery, the cause is the tooth or the gum, not the veneer: decay at the margin from neglected flossing, gum recession exposing a little root, or a grinder without a night guard loading the edges. All three are preventable with normal hygiene, six-monthly cleanings and the guard. [How long porcelain veneers last](/blog/how-long-do-porcelain-veneers-last) has the survival data.

If you have been putting off veneers because you expect them to hurt, the honest summary is this: one injection, three hours of vibration, two days of cold sensitivity, and a week later you have forgotten it. If you want to know how much preparation your own teeth would need, which is the number that decides all of the above, send three photos through the [free photo evaluation](/free-photo-evaluation) and the plan comes back tooth by tooth.

faq.a: No. The numbing injection is a few seconds of pressure after a topical gel, the preparation is done under local anesthesia and stays in enamel, and the bonding visit does not hurt. Afterwards most patients report mild cold sensitivity for two or three days, rated 1 or 2 out of 10, and no pain.

faq.q: Can you get veneers without anesthesia?
faq.a: With 0.3 mm veneers it is possible, because the preparation stays in enamel and never reaches the nerve, and a few patients choose it. We still recommend local anesthesia: three hours in the chair is more comfortable numb, and the injection itself is the only part most people feel.

faq.q: Do veneers hurt more than a filling or a crown?
faq.a: Less. A filling goes through enamel into dentin, and a crown removes 60 to 70% of the tooth, often close to the nerve; both commonly cause sensitivity for days or weeks. A 0.3 mm veneer preparation stays in the outer third of the enamel, so the usual experience is the injection and little else.

faq.q: How long does the numbness last after the veneer appointment?
faq.a: Two to three hours for most people. Your lip and cheek feel large and you should avoid hot drinks and chewing on that side until the feeling returns, so you do not bite yourself. The numbness is the anesthetic wearing off normally, not a sign of anything wrong.

faq.q: Why does my new veneer hurt when I bite?
faq.a: Almost always a high spot: that veneer is meeting the opposing tooth a fraction before the others, so it takes the whole bite force. It is fixed in about five minutes by marking the contact and polishing it, without anesthetic. Call the same day; a high spot left alone is the main reason veneers chip.

faq.q: Is it normal for veneers to hurt years later?
faq.a: No. Porcelain has no nerve. Pain years after delivery comes from the tooth or gum under the veneer: decay at the margin, gum recession or grinding without a night guard. All are preventable with normal hygiene, six-monthly cleanings and the guard, and all are treatable without necessarily replacing the veneer.
